correctness.rationale: The prime-factor escape lemma forces L_m(t)>2m for every t>B_m with gcd(t,P_m)=1. Multiplicativity gives first two iterates; comparing them with p^a proves both strict signs for all a. For m=4, small ell requires t in an exact six-element set, and explicit p29,p59 and small prime computations finish the complete classification. CRT plus the fixed-modulus prime number theorem in progressions gives the exact density. Replayed exact integer computations (987 general and 378 m4 cases) corroborate the claims but are not substitutes for the symbolic proof.

value.rationale: Determines the exact sign for all sufficiently large prime powers at every even parameter and classifies each allowed base residue; the density product is a natural, nontrivial quantitative invariant. The smallest two-sided even case m=4 receives a complete no-perfect-prime-power classification including exceptional small primes. The classification is structurally stronger than merely showing some abundant primes exist, and addresses the original problem of understanding D_m sizes.
